//: THE SURFACE CLOSET (z0).  A perfectly ordinary maintenance room, entered through the article's 'reinforced steel' door, which now simply OPENS - no lockpicking, no smashing.  The door is a real door: furniture_and_terrain/scp_087_shaft_terrain.json gives it an 'open' link so the ordinary 'o' key works from the street.
//2: The '>' threshold at (11,2) carries MON_AVOID_STRICT - the containment boundary, and the ONLY tile in the mod that does.
//3: STAIR-CHAINING RULE (verified: src/game.cpp:9955 and 9976-9981): descending looks for a GOES_UP tile on the level below at the SAME x,y.  So this '>' at (11,2) sits directly above z-1's '<' at (11,2).
//4: THE ENTRANCE IS TWO ROWS DEEP, and that is what makes the knock beat possible.  The door sits at (12,22) with a PASSABLE CONCRETE APRON at (12,23) outside it, instead of the door occupying the very last row.  Reason: the building is a sealed 24x24 overmap tile, so (12,23) is on the OMT boundary - which means stepping onto it is an OMT TRANSITION.  avatar_enters_omt therefore fires exactly as the player walks up to the door, BEFORE it is opened, and that is where EOC_SCP_087_DOOR_KNOCK hangs the 'something knocks from the other side' line.  With the door itself on the boundary you could only ever arrive after opening it, and the beat would land too late.  t_concrete is a core terrain (data/json/furniture_and_terrain/terrain-floors-outdoors.json) so the apron is genuinely OUTDOORS - using the closet floor there would mean an INDOORS flag on an exterior tile and would break the is_outside tests the companion refusal relies on.

//: THE FLIGHT AND THE LANDING (z-1 ONLY as of the loot pass - the other odd depths now have their own copies of these same rows, see the note at the end of this file).  This models the article's staircase literally.
//2: From SCP-087: 'Stairs descend on a 38 degree angle for 13 steps before reaching a semicircular platform of approximately 3 meters in diameter.  Descent direction rotates 180 degrees at each platform.'
//3: - THE FLIGHT is the 3-tile-wide corridor at cols 10-12, running rows 2-14 - that is exactly 13 step tiles, one per described step.
//4: - THE LANDING is the wide open platform at cols 6-16, rows 15-21 (11 tiles across, standing in for the ~3m semicircular platform).  It is floored with t_scp_087_landing, which was previously defined but never used.
//5: - THE 180-DEGREE TURN is real: this level's '<' arrival (11,2) and '>' departure (11,20) are at OPPOSITE ends of the flight, and the NEXT level is mirrored (layout B), so the descent reverses direction every platform.  The straight 13-step run plus the landing is also what limits sight to about 1.5 flights - you see the flight and the start of the platform, and the turn hides the rest.

//: LAYOUT B (even depths: z-2, z-4, z-6, z-8).  Identical geometry to layout A with the two stairs swapped: you arrive at (11,20) and leave from (11,2).  So A's down-stairs sits directly above B's up-stairs and vice versa - a continuous switchback, which is the 180-degree reversal the article describes, expressed as the mirroring between levels.  Because the levels are mirror images the player cannot easily tell them apart, which is the point.

THE DEEPEST AUTHORED LEVEL (z-9).  Layout A, except that where the down-stairs would be there is the SEAM: t_scp_087_seam at (11,20), carrying the invisible tr_scp_087_seam trap.  Stepping onto it fires EOC_SCP_087_SEAM, which increments the loop counter and teleports the player back up the shaft.
//2: This is the whole trick: the map has a bottom, but the player can never reach it, because the bottom quietly returns them to the top.  'It is unknown if SCP-087 has an endpoint' is therefore true in every observable way without the mod pretending to be infinite.
//3: LOOT: this level carries the scavenger's body and the field log, both on the landing - (9,17) and (12,19) - deliberately clear of the seam at (11,20), so either can be picked up on ANY loop, including the reversible loops 1-4, without triggering the descent.  The scavenger rolls at 45% like the other three bodies; the log is the one thing in the shaft that is not random, because it is the reason to reach the bottom.

//: LOOT ADDITIONS: ONE BODY PER ARCHETYPE, ONE ARCHETYPE PER LEVEL.  Two loaded facts shape this, and the first one cost a failed loader run:
//2: (1) A mapgen OBJECT CANNOT BE ITEMS-ONLY.  An object with just an 'items' array fails with 'format: no terrain map' and the game will not start, so every loot placement has to live in a full mapgen object that carries its own rows.  That is why z-3, z-5 and z-7 below duplicate layout A's rows verbatim: they are the same map plus a body.  THIS IS THE MAINTENANCE COST OF THIS FILE - if the shaft geometry ever changes, these three row blocks must change with it.
//3: (2) One mapgen object serves EVERY oter in its om_terrain list, so a body placed inside layout A would have appeared on z-1, z-3, z-5 AND z-7 - four copies of the same researcher.  'One body per archetype' therefore required splitting those levels out of layout A, which is why it now names z-1 alone.  Layout B (z-2/4/6/8) still shares one object and carries no loot.
//4: COORDINATES, verified by a script that reads these very rows (scratchpad loot_audit.py): the flight corridor is cols 10-12, rows 1-14 and the landing is cols 6-16, rows 15-21, so every coordinate below lands on '.' (t_scp_087_floor) or 'L' (t_scp_087_landing).  None touches (11,2) (the '<' up-stairs) or (11,20) (the '>' down-stairs, and on z-9 the 'Q' seam).  A body in a wall would be invisible and the loader would not complain.
//5: CHANCE 45 ON THE BODY IS THE RNG'S FIRST LAYER: three bodies in five exist, so a descent often has fewer than four and a descent with none at all is entirely possible.  The second layer is inside each kit group (items/scp_087_loot.json), where every entry rolls independently.  The corpse is the first entry OF each kit group, so body and gear are one roll - never a kit lying beside no body.
//6: TWO FIELD-NAME TRAPS, both hit during implementation, both fatal rather than silent: (a) COORDINATE placements go in 'place_items', NOT 'items' - 'items' is the symbol-keyed form, and handing it an array of x/y entries gives 'Unread data. Invalid or misplaced field name "items"'; (b) 'place_items' takes an item GROUP id, so pointing it at scp_087_field_log directly gave 'Invalid item_group_id "scp_087_field_log"' (src/mapgen.cpp:2451, jmapgen_item_group::check) and the log is now placed through the one-entry group scp_087_field_log_group.  The bodies did not need that treatment because their kits are groups already.

//: THE SECURITY ESCORT, on z-5, at (12,10) - mid-flight, which is where a body would end up if the person it belonged to was still walking when it happened.
THE SUBJECT, on z-7, at (11,13) - at the bottom of a flight, on the last steps before the landing.  The coordinate was left clear of both stair tiles on purpose.
